messages.subject: simulation with thresholds
parts:
Hello, I am trying to simulate a simple path model with lavaan, using thresholds, but I got this error: 

model <- '
Y ~ .3X + .5*L
Ry ~ 2.4*X + .9*L

Ry | 0*t1 
'

data <- simulateData(model, sample.nobs=10)

Error in names(Data) <- var.names : 
  'names' attribute [3] must be the same length as the vector [1]

What I have been doing to deal with this is to simulate the data using continuous variables (i.e., Ry as continuous variable) and then to define a threshold for Ry (e.g., percentile .75).

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: simulation with thresholds
parts:
On 05/11/2014 01:53 AM, Sebastián Daza wrote:
> Hello, I am trying to simulate a simple path model with lavaan, using
> thresholds, but I got this error:
>
> model <- '
> Y ~ .3X + .5*L
> Ry ~ 2.4*X + .9*L
>
> Ry | 0*t1
> '
>
> data <- simulateData(model, sample.nobs=10)
>
> Error in names(Data) <- var.names :
> 'names' attribute [3] must be the same length as the vector [1]

True. This is a bug in 0.5-16. It happens if you specify thresholds in
the syntax, and you have exogenous covariates.

The best approach here is indeed to simulate the data as if everything
is continuous, and in a second step discretize the categorical variable
using the threshold(s).

Yves.
